extracted.intended_audience: students/scholars of Christian theology; clergy and educated laity interested in ecclesiology and soteriology
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of the threefold office of Christ (Redeemer, Prophet/Teacher, King) and an account of ecclesiastical power: its nature, limits, transmission, relation to civil authority, sacraments, faith, and martyrdom. Intended as doctrinal instruction and practical guidance for ministers and believers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three parts of the Office of Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: We find in Holy Scripture three parts of the Office of the Messiah: the first of a Redeemer, or Saviour; the second of a Pastor, Counsellour, or Teacher (a Prophet sent from God, to convert such as God hath elected to Salvation); the third of a King, and Eternall King, but under his Father.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of the three parts corresponds to different 'times': Redemption wrought at his first coming (sacrifice on the Cross); conversion wrought partly then and now by his ministers until his coming again; the glorious Reign begins after his coming again and lasts eternally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office as Redeemer (requirement of sacrifice and ransom)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the Office of a Redeemer... it appertaineth, that he was Sacrificed, and thereby bare upon his own head, and carryed away from us our iniquities, in such sort as God had required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ransome is Death; the death of the Messiah is a sufficient price for the Sins of all mankind because God accepted it in mercy. Typology from Leviticus 16: one goat sacrificed and one scapegoat; Christ is both the sacrificed Goat (died) and the Scape Goat (resurrection/escape).

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ's kingdom is not of this world
rubrics_metrics.description: My Kingdome is not of this world. The Kingdome of Christ is not to begin till the general Resurrection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Redeemer had no title to rule the redeemed until the Ransome was paid (his death), Christ (as man) was not King of those he redeemed while he walked bodily on earth. Passages cited: John 18:36; Mat. 16:27; Mat. 23:2; Luke 12:14; John 12:47. His present preaching time is an 'earnest' or preparation for the future kingdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of Christ's first coming: renew covenant and persuade the elect
rubrics_metrics.description: The End Of Christs Comming Was To Renew The Covenant Of The Kingdome Of God, And To Perswade The Elect To Imbrace It.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: His first coming restored a new covenant and proclaimed himself the promised Messiah, offered himself in sacrifice, and called those who would believe (including from the Gentiles). Preaching and miracles served to persuade and prepare men for the immortality to come; this 'Regeneration' is not a civil kingdom and does not license disobedience to magistrates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ's preaching was not contrary to Jewish or Roman law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Preaching Of Christ Not Contrary To The Then Law Of The Jews, Nor Of Caesar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He taught obedience to those in Moses' seat and to pay tribute to Caesar; his kingdom was of another world and he did nothing against their laws. Even Pilate pronounced 'I find no fault in him.' Therefore Christ's words/actions were not seditious though enemies used them maliciously.

rubrics_metrics.name: King of the elect after resurrection (nature and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Third Part Of His Office Was To Be King (Under His Father) Of The Elect; his Kingdome was not to begin till the Resurrection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the final coming Christ will reign peculiarly over his elect by virtue of the pact made in Baptism; apostles shall sit on twelve thrones judging tribes of Israel. 'Eating at Christ's table' means enjoying immortality (Tree of Life). He reigns in his human nature then.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ's kingly authority subordinate to the Father
rubrics_metrics.description: Christs Authority In The Kingdome Of God Subordinate To His Father.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christ is a viceregent of the Father (like Moses or the high priests relative to God). Proofs: prayer 'Thy Kingdome come'; 'For thine is the Kingdome, the power and the Glory'; 1 Cor 15:24 'then commeth the end when he shall have delivered up the Kingdome to God.' The human exercise of Christ's kingship is subordinate to the Father.

rubrics_metrics.name: One God represented by Moses, Christ, and Apostles (Trinitarian language as 'persons represented')
rubrics_metrics.description: One And The Same God Is The Person Represented By Moses, And By Christ. God being represented by different 'Representers' may be said to be three Persons though of one Substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument frames 'person' as relative to a representer: Moses represented God in the Old Testament, Christ in his incarnation, and the Apostles and their successors represent God in their preaching. Thus Father, Son, and Holy Spirit arise from times/occurrences of representation rather than explicit Old Testament names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecclesiastical power changes with historical context (distinguish times)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the understanding of POWER ECCLESIASTICALL... we are to distinguish the time from the Ascension of our Saviour, into two parts; one before the Conversion of Kings... the other after their Conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initially (long after Ascension before Christian rulers embraced the faith) power was in Apostles, then in those ordained by them; after conversion of princes the situation altered. Historical timing conditions what ecclesiastical power practically is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of hands as sign of transmission of Holy Spirit and commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposition of hands... was nothing else but the Seal of their Commission to Preach Christ, and teach his Doctrine; and the giving of the Holy Ghost by that ceremony of Imposition of hands, was an imitation of that which Moses did.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apostles received the Spirit by Christ breathing and Pentecost; successors received it (and the power) by successive laying on of hands, analogous to Moses laying hands on Joshua (Deut. 34:9). Thus ministerial authority transmitted by ordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power ecclesiastical is but the power to teach (no coercive spiritual authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Power Ecclesiasticall Is But The Power To Teach: ministers are our Schoolemasters, and not our Commanders, and their Precepts not Laws, but wholesome Counsells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no coercive power is left by our Saviour, then debates about monarchical/aristocratic/democratic forms of ecclesiastical sovereignty are vain. Ministers' role is proclamation and persuasion, not compulsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from Christ's own mission (ministers sent to persuade, not command)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the Kingdome of Christ is not of this world: neither can his Ministers (unlesse they be Kings,) require obedience in his name. As my Father sent me... I send you. But our Saviour was sent to perswade...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since Christ's mission was to persuade Jews and Gentiles to embrace the kingdom, the ministers' authority is persuasive/evangelical rather than coercive or judicial while awaiting the final kingdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regeneration (between Ascension and Resurrection) indicates preparation not reign
rubrics_metrics.description: The time between the Ascension, and the generall Resurrection, is called, not a Reigning, but a Regeneration; that is, a Preparation of men for the second and glorious coming of Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scriptural support: Mat. 19:28 'You that have followed me in the Regeneration...'; Ephes. 6:15 'Preparation of the Gospel of Peace.' This period's metaphors (fishing, leaven, seed) emphasize growth and persuasion rather than dominion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evangelization analogies exclude compulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: The work of Christs Ministers, is Evangelization; it is compared to Fishing, Leaven, Seed... by all which Compulsion is excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christ said 'Fishers of Men' not 'Hunters of Men'; ministry involves proclamation and winning by persuasion, not coercion or punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith's nature excludes coercion (ministers have no power to punish unbelief)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Christs Ministers in this world, is to make men Beleeve... But Faith hath no relation to, nor dependence at all upon Compulsion, or Commandement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers have no power by that title to punish anyone for unbelief or contradiction; they are 'Helpers of your Joy' and 'have no Dominion over your Faith' (2 Cor.1:24). However, if ministers possess civil sovereign power by polity, they may lawfully punish by civil sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority granted to civil princes obliges obedience to secular rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: From The Authority Christ Hath Left To Civill Princes... St. Paul and St. Peter exhort submission to higher powers and governors; 'all Power is ordained of God.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scriptural citations (Col. 3:20; Rom.13; 1 Pet.2:13-15; Tit.3:1) show that obedience is required even to infidel rulers; therefore Christians must obey their lawful sovereigns, and ministers lack authority to command contrary to civil ordinances unless they themselves hold civil power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible external compliance under persecution (distinguishing inner faith and outward acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: What Christians May Do To Avoid Persecution: belief cannot be commanded away; profession with the tongue is an external act distinct from inward faith, and may be performed under compulsion to preserve life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of Naaman (2 Kings 5:17): outward acts under sovereign compulsion may be pardoned. If a subject is compelled by lawful prince to perform external acts contrary to inward belief, the action is the sovereign's, not the subject's. The example argues prudential obedience rather than unnecessary self-sacrifice where not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and proper object of martyrdom
rubrics_metrics.description: A Martyr is a Witnesse of the Resurrection of Jesus the Messiah; which none can be but those that conversed with him on earth, and saw him after he was risen... none but such can properly be called Martyrs of Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only original disciples who were eyewitnesses of Christ's resurrection are primary martyrs; those who suffer for belief in witnesses are 'secondary' martyrs. Dying for other doctrines or for clergy ambition/profit is not true martyrdom. Only the article 'Jesus Is The Christ' merits that name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of obligation to suffer (only those sent and called to preach)
rubrics_metrics.description: He that is not sent to preach this fundamentall article, but taketh it upon him of his private authority... yet is he not obliged to suffer death for that cause; because being not called thereto, tis not required at his hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those formally commissioned to preach to unbelievers may lawfully suffer as martyrs; private persons not sent by commission are not bound to suffer martyrdom for that mission. The apostolic commission's scope matters for obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of the Apostolic commission contain no authority over the congregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lastly the points of their Commission, as they are expressely set down in the Gospel, contain none of them any authority over the Congregation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter begins to enumerate 'To Preach' etc., implying that the commissions given are missionary/evangelical rather than grants of coercive governance over congregations.
